result.summary: Adds an optional `keypath_only` boolean parameter (default `false`) to `send`, `sendall`, `walletcreatefundedpsbt`, `walletprocesspsbt`, and `descriptorprocesspsbt`. When enabled, the wallet and signing logic populate only Taproot key-path data, skip creating script-path signatures, and refuse to finalize transactions via script paths.
result.problem: When spending from Taproot outputs that have both key paths and script trees (such as MuSig2 setups with recovery or timelocked script fallbacks), the wallet automatically populates and signs for script paths. This can trigger hardware signer bugs, increases fee overhead, leaks privacy by prematurely revealing fallback scripts, and risks accidental on-chain fallback execution when co-signers could have spent cooperatively via the key path.
evidence: PR description: 'While testing MuSig2 integration in #29675 I ran into a Ledger bug https://github.com/LedgerHQ/app-bitcoin-new/issues/329 that was triggered because we signed for a script path in addition to the key path.'

PR description: 'For example, you may have a 2-of-2 musig() descriptor with some sort of fallback after coins are N blocks old. For both on chain privacy and fee reasons, you don't want to use this path unless absolutely necessary. But our wallet can't know if our co-signer still has their key, so we sign the script path at all times. This could lead to accidental broadcast.'
result.changed_since_previous: Added explicit error handling and tests to reject `keypath_only` if passed to `fundrawtransaction`, and added a release note.
result.card: Adds a keypath_only option to send, sendall, walletcreatefundedpsbt, walletprocesspsbt, and descriptorprocesspsbt to restrict Taproot spending to key paths. When enabled, the signing and PSBT filling logic will not add script-path data, will not produce script-path signatures, and will refuse to finalize script paths. This prevents accidental on-chain disclosure of fallback branches (such as in MuSig2 descriptors with timelocked recovery scripts), avoids paying higher script-path fees unnecessarily, and avoids triggering firmware bugs in hardware signing devices.

risk.why: A flaw in signature creation or PSBT finalization controls could prevent signing or unintentionally omit required signatures, causing transaction creation to fail for users of complex Taproot descriptors.
